### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. PHARC syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.445)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-426048)

**Proposed mechanism:** ABHD12 (HGNC:25720) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal hydrolase activity (GO:0005759); Lysosomal hydrolase activity (GO:0005759) —LEADS_TO→ Ataxia (HP:0001251); Lysosomal hydrolase activity (GO:0005759) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal head movements (HP:0000484); Lysosomal hydrolase activity (GO:0005759) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebellar hypoplasia (HP:0001304). Loss-of-function mutations in ABHD12 disrupt its lysosomal hydrolase activity, leading to downstream phenotypic consequences including ataxia, abnormal head movements, and cerebellar hypoplasia, common to both benign paroxysmal tonic upgaze of childhood with ataxia and PHARC syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ABHD12 that lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects in either disease would falsify the proposed loss-of-function mechanism. Furthermore, if mutations in DAGLA were found to cause one of these conditions independently without affecting ABHD12 function, it would suggest a separate mechanistic link. _(variant: High frequency (>1%) of pathogenic ABHD12 variants in gnomAD populations would suggest incomplete penetrance or alternative explanations for the observed phenotypes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ABHD12 in these disorders could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring lysosomal hydrolase function or mitigating downstream neurological damage, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
